CODE
Art. 2.3.49.
Discharge of the debt of reward
A spouse who is still liable to pay a reward, discharges it, either by taking less, or by payment to the estate to be partitioned, in an amount equal to the amount of his or her debt.
Discharge in lesser sum is made either by deduction from the share of the debtor spouse or by deduction by his or her spouse.
A spouse who is still entitled to a reward deducts from the assets to be shared an amount equal to the value of his or her claim.
In the absence of agreement between the spouses as to the application of paragraph 1 or paragraph 2, and in particular as to the designation of the assets which may be deducted, the dispute shall be settled in the context of the judicial partition procedure.
Unless agreed by the spouses, the levy may not affect the rights of attribution granted to the other spouse by Articles 2.3.13 and 2.3.14.
A spouse who has not been able to obtain the full amount of his or her reward from the estate becomes a creditor of the other spouse for half of what he or she has not received.
